## Installation

```bash
pip install iii-sdk
```

## Initialization

### register_worker

Register the worker with a iii instance, returns a connected worker client.

Blocks up to 30 seconds for the WebSocket connection to be established.
If the engine is not reachable in time, a warning is logged and the
client is returned anyway; it keeps retrying in the background and
flushes registrations once connected. Use
``add_connection_state_listener`` to observe the actual transition.

**Signature**

```python
register_worker(address: str | None = None, options: InitOptions | None = None) -> III
```

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Parameters">

<ParamField body="address" type="str | None">
  WebSocket URL of the III engine (e.g. ``ws://localhost:49134``). When omitted, resolves from ``III_URL`` and then ``DEFAULT_ENGINE_URL``.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="options" type="InitOptions | None">
  Optional configuration for worker name, timeouts, reconnection, and OTel.

  <Expandable title="`InitOptions` fields">
    <ParamField body="enable_metrics_reporting" type="bool">
      Enable worker metrics via OpenTelemetry. Default ``True``.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="headers" type="dict[str, str] | None">
      Custom HTTP headers sent during the WebSocket handshake, on the main connection and on streaming channels. ``Authorization: Bearer $III_TOKEN`` is added unless you set ``Authorization`` here.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="invocation_timeout_ms" type="int">
      Default timeout for ``worker.call()`` invocations in milliseconds. Default ``30000``.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="namespace" type="str | None">
      Namespace this worker belongs to. Falls back to the ``III_NAMESPACE`` env var; when neither is set the engine applies ``default``. It scopes more than the registration: the worker and its functions register here, and everything the worker does afterwards follows it: ``call`` resolves its target here and ``observe`` resolves its source and target here, unless the call names another namespace.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="otel" type="OtelConfig | dict[str, Any] | None">
      OpenTelemetry configuration. Enabled by default. Set ``{'enabled': False}`` or env ``OTEL_ENABLED=false`` to disable.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="reconnection_config" type="ReconnectionConfig | None">
      WebSocket reconnection behavior.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="telemetry" type="TelemetryOptions | None">
      Internal worker metadata reported to the engine.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="worker_description" type="str | None">
      One-line, human/LLM-readable summary of what this worker does. Surfaces in ``engine::workers::list`` / ``engine::workers::info``.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="worker_name" type="str | None">
      Display name for this worker. A non-empty ``III_WORKER_NAME`` overrides it. Defaults to ``hostname:pid``.
    </ParamField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>


  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Example">

```python
from iii import register_worker, InitOptions
worker = register_worker()  # address from III_URL
other = register_worker('ws://localhost:49134', InitOptions(worker_name='my-worker'))
```

## Methods

### register_function

Register a function with the engine.

Pass a handler for local execution, or an ``HttpInvocationConfig``
for HTTP-invoked functions (Lambda, Cloudflare Workers, etc.).

Handlers can be synchronous or asynchronous.  Sync handlers are
automatically wrapped with ``run_in_executor`` so they do not
block the event loop.  Each handler receives a ``data`` argument
containing the call's payload, and may optionally accept a second
``metadata`` argument carrying per-invocation metadata (e.g.
``def handler(data, metadata=None)`` or ``def handler(data, *,
metadata=None)``).  Metadata is only forwarded to handlers that
declare a parameter literally named ``metadata``, so existing
handlers, including ones with unrelated extra parameters,
``*args``, or ``**kwargs``, keep working unchanged.

The handler's return value is what the function's observers observe.
An event source's handler returns the event it is called with. What
this worker does when the function is observed is set with the hook
methods (``on_observer_added``, ``on_observer_removed``,
``on_observer_match``, ``on_observer_deliver``) on the client by id or
on the returned ``FunctionRef``. Set ``on_observer_added`` and
``on_observer_removed`` by id before registering so they run for every
observer: the engine may announce an observer before a hook set on the
``FunctionRef`` is in place.

``request_format`` and ``response_format`` are auto-extracted
from the handler's type hints when omitted or passed as ``None``
(the default).  To opt out of auto-extraction, pass an explicit
schema (``RegisterFunctionFormat`` or ``dict``).  This behavior
is Python-specific; the Node SDK relies on explicit schemas because
TypeScript types are erased at runtime.

**Signature**

```python
register_function(function_id: str, handler_or_invocation: RemoteFunctionHandler | HttpInvocationConfig, *, description: str | None = None, metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None, request_format: RegisterFunctionFormat | dict[str, Any] | None = None, response_format: RegisterFunctionFormat | dict[str, Any] | None = None, args_format: Any = None, private: bool = False, observable: bool = True, standby: bool = False, local_dispatch: bool = True) -> FunctionRef
```

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Parameters">

<ParamField body="function_id" type="str" required>
  Unique string identifier for the function.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="handler_or_invocation" type="RemoteFunctionHandler | HttpInvocationConfig" required>
  A callable handler or ``HttpInvocationConfig``.  Callable handlers receive ``data`` (the call's payload) as the first argument and may optionally accept ``metadata`` (per-invocation metadata) as a second argument; they may return a value.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="description" type="str | None">
  Human-readable description of what the function does.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="metadata" type="dict[str, Any] | None">
  Arbitrary metadata attached to the function.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="request_format" type="RegisterFunctionFormat | dict[str, Any] | None">
  Schema describing expected input.  When ``None`` (default), auto-extracted from the handler's first-parameter type hint.  Pass an explicit schema to override; there is no way to register with no schema when the handler is typed.

  <Expandable title="`RegisterFunctionFormat` fields">
    <ParamField body="body" type="list[RegisterFunctionFormat] | None">
      Nested fields for object types.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="description" type="str | None">
      Human-readable description of the parameter.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="items" type="RegisterFunctionFormat | None">
      Item schema for array types.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="name" type="str" required>
      Parameter name.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="required" type="bool">
      Whether the parameter is required.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="type" type="str" required>
      Type string (``string``, ``number``, ``boolean``, ``object``, ``array``, ``null``, ``map``).
    </ParamField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="response_format" type="RegisterFunctionFormat | dict[str, Any] | None">
  Schema describing the handler's return value, what observers observe.  Same auto-extraction semantics as ``request_format``.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="args_format" type="Any">
  JSON Schema (or a Pydantic model) of the observers' ``args``; the engine validates them (``INVALID_ARGS``). A function without it takes no args.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="private" type="bool">
  Only this worker may call the function; others may observe it. This worker's own calls pass the input and the result by reference: the handler and hooks treat both as read-only.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="observable" type="bool">
  ``False``: nobody may observe the function (``NOT_OBSERVABLE``), for functions whose payloads carry credentials.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="standby" type="bool">
  When another worker already hosts the id (``FUNCTION_NAMESPACE_CONFLICT``), retry every second (±20 %) and take the function over when that worker leaves.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="local_dispatch" type="bool">
  Calls this worker makes to its own function run in-process once the engine confirmed it (default ``True``). Like a remote invocation, each local call to a sync handler runs on a thread of its own (one per call, not pooled), so the caller can stop waiting at its timeout. A sync handler that blocks for long should be async, or set ``False`` so its calls go through the engine (also for a handler that relies on engine-side effects).
</ParamField>


  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Example">

```python
def greet(data):
    return {'message': f"Hello, {data['name']}!"}
fn = worker.register_function("greet", greet, description="Greets a user")
fn.unregister()
from pydantic import BaseModel
class GreetInput(BaseModel):
    name: str
class GreetOutput(BaseModel):
    message: str
async def greet(data: GreetInput) -> GreetOutput:
    return GreetOutput(message=f"Hello, {data.name}!")
fn = worker.register_function("greet", greet, description="Greets a user")
on_tick = worker.register_function(
    "cron::on-tick", lambda tick: tick, args_format=CronArgs, private=True
)
```

### call

Call a function and return its result.



The routing behavior and return type depend on the ``action`` field:

- No action: synchronous, waits for the function to return.
- ``CallAction.Enqueue(...)``: async via named queue, returns a dict
  with ``messageReceiptId``.
- ``CallAction.Void()``: fire-and-forget, returns ``None``.

A function this worker registered with a handler, once the engine
confirmed it, runs in-process (local dispatch): a sync handler on a
thread of its own (the caller waits up to the timeout), an async one
on the SDK loop. Its observers are still delivered to, and only
matched calls reach the engine. ``dispatch="remote"`` (or
``action=Enqueue``) always goes through the engine. Whatever a local
handler raises, ``BaseException``s such as ``KeyboardInterrupt`` and
``SystemExit`` included, reaches the caller as
``InvocationError("invocation_failed")`` with the original as its
``__cause__`` (for a ``Void`` call nothing reaches the caller: the
error is logged).

``metadata`` is any JSON value; the handler receives it beside the
payload, and ``None`` is no metadata.

A request with ``observer`` (an `Observer` of a function this
worker hosts) calls through it: the engine runs the observer's target
with its policy (``max_fires``, expiry, ``max_in_flight``), metadata
sidecar and loop guard, and the call resolves to the target's result.
It takes no ``metadata``: the target's metadata argument is the
observer's registration metadata, and a request that names metadata
raises ``ValueError`` before anything is sent.
The payload goes as given: filters are applied where the worker
chooses observers: iii's delivery, or ``obs.matches(call)`` in an
``on_observer_deliver``. A call through an observer belongs in that
deliver hook; to send one observer something outside delivery (its
initial state), call the function with ``"metadata": {"for_observer":
obs.id}`` (see `Observer.accepted`).

**Signature**

```python
call(request: dict[str, Any] | CallRequest) -> Any
```

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Parameters">

<ParamField body="request" type="dict[str, Any] | CallRequest" required>
  A ``CallRequest`` or dict with ``function_id`` (or ``observer``), ``payload``, and optional ``action`` / ``timeout_ms`` / ``metadata`` / ``namespace`` / ``dispatch`` (``"auto"``, the default, or ``"remote"``).

  <Expandable title="`CallRequest` fields" defaultOpen>
    <ParamField body="action" type="CallActionEnqueue | CallActionVoid | None">
      Sets how the call is routed. Omit for a synchronous request/response. Specify for a specific routing scheme (e.g. ``CallAction.Enqueue(...)``, ``CallAction.Void()``).
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="dispatch" type="Literal['auto', 'remote'] | None">
      ``auto`` (default) runs a function this worker hosts in-process once the engine confirmed it; ``remote`` always goes through the engine.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="function_id" type="str | None">
      ID of the function to call.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="metadata" type="Any | None">
      Per-invocation metadata (any JSON value) supplied to the called handler beside the payload. ``None`` is no metadata.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="namespace" type="str | None">
      Target namespace for routing. Omit to inherit this worker's; say ``default`` to reach the engine's from a namespaced worker.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="observer" type="Any">
      An `Observer` of a function this worker hosts: the call runs its target, with its policy and metadata sidecar. Takes no ``function_id``, ``namespace``, ``metadata`` or enqueue action.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="payload" type="Any">
      Input data passed to the function.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="timeout_ms" type="int | None">
      Override the default invocation timeout, in milliseconds.
    </ParamField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>


  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Example">

```python
result = worker.call({'function_id': 'greet', 'payload': {'name': 'World'}})
worker.call({'function_id': 'notify', 'payload': {}, 'action': CallAction.Void()})
worker.call({'observer': obs, 'payload': request})  # in a deliver hook
```


  </Tab>
</Tabs>

### observe

Observes a function: when ``source`` runs, ``target`` runs. Every
call of the source function that passes ``source["filters"]`` invokes
``target``, a registered function, with the ``Observed`` envelope
(``input``, ``output`` or ``error``, ``caller``, ...);
``source["deliver"]`` set to ``"input"`` or ``"output"`` gives it that
value instead. The worker that hosts the source can decide otherwise
in its ``on_observer_deliver``.

Returns synchronously, also before the connection is up; the observer
is replayed with the same id on every reconnect. The handle holds its
id until its ``dispose()`` is called or the engine disposes it; the
id is free again at once after that. Errors
(``INVALID_ARGS``, ``INVALID_FILTER``, ``FORBIDDEN``,
``NOT_OBSERVABLE``, the rejection of the source's worker,
``UNSUPPORTED`` against an engine without observe) show up as state
``error`` and make ``ready()`` raise `ObserveRejection`. The
engine's refusal is the handle's final answer: it is not replayed,
it holds its id until its ``dispose()``, and that ``dispose()``
sends nothing.

**Signature**

```python
observe(source: str | ObserveSource | dict[str, Any], target: Target, options: ObserverOptions | dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> ObserverHandle
```

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Parameters">

<ParamField body="source" type="str | ObserveSource | dict[str, Any]" required>
  What is observed: a function id, or ``function_id``, ``namespace``, ``args`` (read by the worker that hosts the function, validated against its ``args_format``), ``filters``, and ``on`` / ``capture`` / ``deliver``.

  <Expandable title="`ObserveSource` fields">
    <ParamField body="function_id" type="str" required>
      The observed function.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="args" type="dict[str, Any]">
      For the worker that hosts the function, which reads them in its hooks; validated against the function's ``args_format``. A function without ``args_format`` takes none.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="capture" type="list[Capture]">
      Default ``["input", "output", "caller"]``.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="deliver" type="Literal['envelope', 'input', 'output']">
      What the target receives when iii delivers: ``"envelope"`` (default), ``"input"`` or ``"output"``.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="filters" type="Filter">
      Which calls reach the target; ``{}`` (or absent) = every call.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="namespace" type="str">
      Defaults to this worker's (``engine::*`` resolves to ``default``).
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="on" type="Literal['success', 'error', 'complete']">
      ``"success"`` (default), ``"error"`` or ``"complete"``.
    </ParamField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="target" type="Target" required>
  The function to invoke: its id, or ``{"function_id": ..., "namespace": ...}``. Register it first; until then the observer stays ``pending``.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="options" type="ObserverOptions | dict[str, Any] | None">
  ``id``, ``max_fires``, ``expires_in_ms``, ``max_in_flight``, ``metadata`` (the activation's metadata sidecar).

  <Expandable title="`ObserverOptions` fields">
    <ParamField body="expires_in_ms" type="int">
      Disposed after this long.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="id" type="str">
      Default: a random UUID, stable across replays.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="max_fires" type="int">
      Disposed after this many activations.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="max_in_flight" type="int">
      Activations running at once (the engine queues the rest).
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="metadata" type="dict[str, Any]">
      Delivered as the metadata sidecar of every activation.
    </ParamField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>


  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Example">

```python
iii.observe("orders::create", "alerts::big-order")
iii.register_function("alerts::payment-failed", notify)
failures = iii.observe(
    {"function_id": "payments::charge", "on": "error",
     "filters": {"input.amount": {"$gte": 500}}},
    "alerts::payment-failed",
    {"max_in_flight": 4},
)
failures.ready()            # or: await failures.ready_async()
failures.dispose()
```


  </Tab>
</Tabs>

### add_connection_state_listener

Subscribe to connection-state transitions.

The handler is fired immediately with the current state (on the
caller's thread), then once per transition. Transitions fire on the
SDK's background event-loop thread: keep handlers fast and do not
call sync SDK methods from them (they would raise ``RuntimeError``).
Treat calls as state notifications, not edges. A state may rarely
be observed twice around subscription. Registering the same handler
twice fires it twice. Returns an idempotent unsubscribe function
that removes only its own registration.

**Signature**

```python
add_connection_state_listener(handler: ConnectionStateCallback) -> Callable[[], None]
```

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Parameters">

<ParamField body="handler" type="ConnectionStateCallback" required>
</ParamField>


  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Example">

```python
unsubscribe = worker.add_connection_state_listener(
    lambda state: print(f"engine link: {state}")
)
```


  </Tab>
</Tabs>

### call_async

Call a function and return its result (on any event loop).

The routing behavior and return type depend on the ``action`` field:

- No action: synchronous, waits for the function to return.
- ``CallAction.Enqueue(...)``: async via named queue, returns a dict
  with ``messageReceiptId``.
- ``CallAction.Void()``: fire-and-forget, returns ``None``.

A function this worker registered with a handler, once the engine
confirmed it, runs in-process on the calling loop (a sync handler on
a thread of its own); ``dispatch="remote"`` (or ``action=Enqueue``)
always goes through the engine. A request with ``observer`` calls
through it, as for `call`.

**Signature**

```python
async (request: dict[str, Any] | CallRequest) -> Any
```

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Parameters">

<ParamField body="request" type="dict[str, Any] | CallRequest" required>

    <ParamField body="action" type="CallActionEnqueue | CallActionVoid | None">

    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="dispatch" type="Literal['auto', 'remote'] | None">
      ``auto`` (default) runs a function this worker hosts in-process once the engine confirmed it; ``remote`` always goes through the engine.
    </ParamField>

    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="metadata" type="Any | None">

      Target namespace for routing. Omit to inherit this worker's; say ``default`` to reach the engine's from a namespaced worker.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="observer" type="Any">
      An `Observer` of a function this worker hosts: the call runs its target, with its policy and metadata sidecar. Takes no ``function_id``, ``namespace``, ``metadata`` or enqueue action.

### connect_async

Connect to the III Engine via WebSocket.

Initializes OpenTelemetry (if configured), attaches the event loop,
and establishes the WebSocket connection. This is called automatically
during construction; use it only if you need to reconnect manually
from an async context.

**Signature**

```python
async () -> None
```

### current_invocation

The invocation the calling code runs in (in every handler, remote or
local), or ``None`` outside any handler.

**Signature**

```python
current_invocation() -> InvocationContext | None
```

#### Example

```python
def create_order(order):
    inv = iii.current_invocation()  # function_id, invocation_id, caller, observe_depth
    return {"id": inv.invocation_id if inv else None}
```

### get_address

Return the engine address this worker resolved to.

The explicit ``register_worker`` argument, else ``III_URL``, else
`DEFAULT_ENGINE_URL`. Mirrors the Rust SDK's ``address()`` and the
Node SDK's ``getAddress()``.

**Signature**

```python
get_address() -> str
```

### get_connection_state

Return the current WebSocket connection state.

**Signature**

```python
get_connection_state() -> IIIConnectionState
```

#### Example

```python
worker = register_worker("ws://localhost:49134")
if worker.get_connection_state() != "connected":
    print("engine not reachable yet")
```

### is_observed

Whether a call of a function this worker hosts would reach anyone,
so a source can skip building an event nobody wants.

Without ``call``: whether the function has any active observer (one
load). With ``call`` (a `Call` or a partial one,
``{"input": ...}``) on a function matched by keys
(``on_observer_match``): whether an observer is filed under one of
the call's keys. On any other function the call is ignored.

**Signature**

```python
is_observed(function_id: str, call: CallLike | None = None) -> bool
```

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Parameters">

<ParamField body="function_id" type="str" required>
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="call" type="CallLike | None">
</ParamField>


  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Example">

```python
if iii.is_observed("database::on-row-changed", {"input": change}):
    iii.call({"function_id": "database::on-row-changed", "payload": change})
```

### on_observer_added

Sets what runs when an observer is added, before it is accepted:
for every function this worker hosts (``on_observer_added(hook)``), or
for one (``on_observer_added("fn::id", hook)``). Works as a decorator,
``@iii.on_observer_added`` or ``@iii.on_observer_added("fn::id")``, and
returns the hook; ``None`` removes it.

The worker's hook runs, then the function's; the observer is accepted
(acked, then active) once both resolved. A hook that raises rejects
the observer with the `ObserveRejection` it raised, or
``OBSERVE_REJECTED``; one still running after 30 s rejects it with
``OWNER_TIMEOUT``. Then the ``on_observer_removed`` of each level whose
hook already resolved runs. Hooks may be sync (on a thread of their
own) or async, and the hooks of one function run one at a time.

Hooks are stored by function id, so they can be set before the
function is registered (which makes them run for every observer) and
stay in place across ``unregister()``. A hook set while the function
already has active observers runs for each of them at once (a raise
rejects that observer) and logs one warning. A second after the
connection is registered, and after the last hook set by id, a
warning names each hook id this worker has not registered.

**Signature**

```python
on_observer_added(function_id_or_hook: Any, hook: Any = ...) -> Any
```

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Parameters">

<ParamField body="function_id_or_hook" type="Any" required>
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="hook" type="Any">
</ParamField>


  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Example">

```python
@iii.on_observer_added            # every function this worker hosts
async def retain(obs):
    await events.retain()
@iii.on_observer_added("cron::on-tick")
def start(obs):
    scheduler.retain(obs.args["expression"])
```


  </Tab>
</Tabs>

---

### on_observer_deliver

Delivers each call of one function itself: ``hook(call,
observers)`` receives the `Call` and the observers that matched
it (``on_observer_match``, or all of them), as a snapshot taken when
the call started, and what it returns (or raises) is what the caller
gets back. iii delivers nothing for that function: the hook calls
through observers (``iii.call({"observer": obs, ...})``) and applies
their ``on`` and filters with ``obs.matches(call)``. Works as a
decorator (``@iii.on_observer_deliver("fn::id")``) and returns the
hook; ``None`` restores iii's delivery.

The hook runs inside the function's invocation, so the calls it makes
have that invocation as their caller. A sync hook runs on a thread of
its own. A function with a deliver hook needs an engine with
``observe.v2``.

**Signature**

```python
on_observer_deliver(function_id: str, hook: Any = ...) -> Any
```

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Parameters">

<ParamField body="function_id" type="str" required>
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="hook" type="Any">
</ParamField>


  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Example">

```python
@iii.on_observer_deliver("http::on-request")
async def route(call, observers):
    obs = routes.match(call.input)
    if obs is None:
        return {"status_code": 404}
    if not obs.matches(call):
        return {"status_code": 422}
    return await iii.call_async({"observer": obs, "payload": call.input})
```


  </Tab>
</Tabs>

---

### on_observer_match

Sets which observers want each call of one function. By default
every observer wants every call; iii's delivery then applies their
``on`` and filters, and an ``on_observer_deliver`` receives only the
observers that matched.

As a predicate, ``hook(obs, call) -> bool`` is asked once per active
observer per call, before filters; a predicate that raises counts as
no match. As keys, ``observer=`` and ``call=`` key functions each
return a string or strings, and an observer wants a call when they
share a key: the SDK computes an observer's keys once, when it is
accepted, and files it under each, so a call costs one lookup per key
whatever the number of observers. An observer whose key function
raises is rejected (``OBSERVE_REJECTED``); a call whose key function
raises matches no observer. A match hook that raises is logged once
per function. Wildcards are keys too: file an observer of every table
under ``"primary|*|insert"`` and give a change the keys
``"primary|orders|insert"``, ``"primary|orders|*"``,
``"primary|*|insert"`` and ``"primary|*|*"``.

A host that sends one observer something of its own (its initial
state) calls the function with ``"metadata": {"for_observer":
obs.id}``, and the hook gives such a call to that observer alone: a
predicate compares the ids, and key functions also file each observer
under ``f"for_observer:{obs.id}"`` and give such a call that one key.

Works as a decorator for a predicate
(``@iii.on_observer_match("fn::id")``) and returns the hook (a
`MatchKeys` for the keys form); ``None`` removes it. A match
hook set while the function has active observers is applied to them
on the SDK loop, which rebuilds the index from them. Predicates and
key functions are sync: they run on every call. A function with a
match hook needs an engine with ``observe.v2``: against an older one
it stays unregistered, and ``UNSUPPORTED`` is logged once.

**Signature**

```python
on_observer_match(function_id: str, hook: Any = ..., *, observer: Any = None, call: Any = None) -> Any
```

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Parameters">

<ParamField body="function_id" type="str" required>
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="hook" type="Any">
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="observer" type="Any">
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="call" type="Any">
</ParamField>


  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Example">

```python
iii.on_observer_match(
    "cron::on-tick", lambda obs, call: obs.args["expression"] == call.input["expression"]
)
iii.on_observer_match(
    "database::on-row-changed",
    observer=lambda obs: f"{obs.args['table']}|{obs.args['op']}",
    call=lambda call: f"{call.input['table']}|{call.input['op']}",
)
```


  </Tab>
</Tabs>

---

### on_observer_removed

Sets what runs when an accepted observer goes (on ``unobserve``, on
disposal, after a late rejection): for every function this worker
hosts, or for one. The same forms as `on_observer_added`.

It runs exactly once for every accepted observer, the function's hook
and then the worker's, and never for an observer that was not
accepted. An error it raises is logged; the observer is removed
either way.

**Signature**

```python
on_observer_removed(function_id_or_hook: Any, hook: Any = ...) -> Any
```

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Parameters">

<ParamField body="function_id_or_hook" type="Any" required>
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="hook" type="Any">
</ParamField>


  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Example">

```python
iii.on_observer_removed(lambda obs: events.release())
@iii.on_observer_removed("cron::on-tick")
def stop(obs):
    scheduler.release(obs.args["expression"])
```


  </Tab>
</Tabs>

---

### shutdown

Gracefully shut down the client, releasing all resources.

Cancels any pending reconnection attempts, rejects all in-flight
invocations with an error, closes the WebSocket connection, and
stops the background event-loop thread.  After this call the
instance must not be reused.

**Signature**

```python
shutdown() -> None
```

#### Example

```python
worker = register_worker('ws://localhost:49134')
# ... do work ...
worker.shutdown()
```


---

### shutdown_async

Gracefully shut down the client, releasing all resources.

Cancels any pending reconnection attempts, rejects all in-flight
invocations with an error, closes the WebSocket connection, and
stops the background event-loop thread.  After this call the
instance must not be reused.

**Signature**

```python
async () -> None
```

#### Example

```python
worker = register_worker('ws://localhost:49134')
# ... do work ...
await worker.shutdown_async()
```

### trigger_async

<Warning>
  **Deprecated since 0.26.0.** Use `call_async`.
</Warning>

Call a function: `call_async` under its 0.25 name.

**Signature**

```python
async (request: dict[str, Any] | CallRequest) -> Any
```

#### Parameters

<ParamField body="request" type="dict[str, Any] | CallRequest" required>

  <Expandable title="`CallRequest` fields">
    <ParamField body="action" type="CallActionEnqueue | CallActionVoid | None">
      Sets how the call is routed. Omit for a synchronous request/response. Specify for a specific routing scheme (e.g. ``CallAction.Enqueue(...)``, ``CallAction.Void()``).
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="dispatch" type="Literal['auto', 'remote'] | None">
      ``auto`` (default) runs a function this worker hosts in-process once the engine confirmed it; ``remote`` always goes through the engine.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="function_id" type="str | None">
      ID of the function to call.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="metadata" type="Any | None">
      Per-invocation metadata (any JSON value) supplied to the called handler beside the payload. ``None`` is no metadata.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="namespace" type="str | None">
      Target namespace for routing. Omit to inherit this worker's; say ``default`` to reach the engine's from a namespaced worker.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="observer" type="Any">
      An `Observer` of a function this worker hosts: the call runs its target, with its policy and metadata sidecar. Takes no ``function_id``, ``namespace``, ``metadata`` or enqueue action.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="payload" type="Any">
      Input data passed to the function.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="timeout_ms" type="int | None">
      Override the default invocation timeout, in milliseconds.
    </ParamField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>


## Types

### iii

[`Call`](#call) · [`CallAction`](#callaction) · [`CallActionEnqueue`](#callactionenqueue) · [`CallActionVoid`](#callactionvoid) · [`Caller`](#caller) · [`EnqueueResult`](#enqueueresult) · [`InitOptions`](#initoptions) · [`InvocationContext`](#invocationcontext) · [`MatchKeys`](#matchkeys) · [`MiddlewareFunctionInput`](#middlewarefunctioninput) · [`Observed`](#observed) · [`Observer`](#observer) · [`ObserverHandle`](#observerhandle) · [`ObserverOptions`](#observeroptions) · [`ObserveSource`](#observesource) · [`StreamRequest`](#streamrequest) · [`StreamResponse`](#streamresponse) · [`TelemetryOptions`](#telemetryoptions)

#### Call

One call of a function, as its observers observe it and its
``on_observer_match`` and ``on_observer_deliver`` hooks receive it.

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `caller` | `dict[str, Any] \| None` | No | Who made the call: ``\{worker_id?, worker_name?, function_id?, invocation_id?, parent?\}``; ``None`` outside any handler. |
| `error` | `dict[str, Any] \| None` | No | What the handler raised, ``\{code, message, stacktrace?\}`` (``None`` when it returned). |
| `function_id` | `str` | Yes | The called function. |
| `input` | `InputT` | Yes | What the function was called with, as the caller passed it (channel refs as refs, not readers and writers). |
| `invocation_id` | `str` | Yes | This call's id. |
| `metadata` | `Any` | No | The call's metadata sidecar. |
| `output` | `OutputT \| None` | No | The handler's return value: what observers observe (``None`` when it raised). |
| `status` | `Literal['success', 'error']` | Yes | ``"success"`` or ``"error"``. |

---

#### CallAction

Factory for creating call actions used with ``call()``.

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Enqueue` | (*, queue: str) -&gt; [`CallActionEnqueue`](#callactionenqueue) | Yes | Route the invocation through a named queue for async processing. |
| `Void` | () -&gt; [`CallActionVoid`](#callactionvoid) | Yes | Fire-and-forget routing. No response is returned. |

---

#### CallActionEnqueue

Routes the call through a named queue for async processing.

Requires the ``queue`` worker in ``worker-compose.yaml`` and a matching
entry under that worker's ``queue_configs``.
Without it the call rejects with ``enqueue_error`` (no queue provider).

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `queue` | `str` | Yes | Name of the target queue. |
| `type` | `Literal['enqueue']` | No | Always ``'enqueue'``. |

---

#### CallActionVoid

Fire-and-forget routing. No response is returned.

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `Literal['void']` | No | Always ``'void'``. |

---

#### Caller

Who started an invocation: the worker (``worker_id`` / ``worker_name``,
stamped by the engine), and the function and invocation the call was made
from (absent for top-level calls). ``parent`` is that handler's own caller,
one level only.

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `function_id` | `str` | No | - |
| `invocation_id` | `str` | No | - |
| `worker_id` | `str` | No | - |
| `worker_name` | `str` | No | - |
| `parent` | `CallerParent` | No | - |

---

#### EnqueueResult

Result returned when a function is called with ``CallAction.Enqueue``.

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `messageReceiptId` | `str` | Yes | Unique receipt ID for the enqueued message. |

#### InitOptions

Configuration options passed to ``register_worker``.

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enable_metrics_reporting` | `bool` | No | Enable worker metrics via OpenTelemetry. Default ``True``. |
| `headers` | `dict[str, str] \| None` | No | Custom HTTP headers sent during the WebSocket handshake, on the main connection and on streaming channels. ``Authorization: Bearer $III_TOKEN`` is added unless you set ``Authorization`` here. |
| `invocation_timeout_ms` | `int` | No | Default timeout for ``worker.call()`` invocations in milliseconds. Default ``30000``. |
| `namespace` | `str \| None` | No | Namespace this worker belongs to. Falls back to the ``III_NAMESPACE`` env var; when neither is set the engine applies ``default``. It scopes more than the registration: the worker and its functions register here, and everything the worker does afterwards follows it: ``call`` resolves its target here and ``observe`` resolves its source and target here, unless the call names another namespace. |
| `otel` | `OtelConfig \| dict[str, Any] \| None` | No | OpenTelemetry configuration. Enabled by default. Set ``\{'enabled': False\}`` or env ``OTEL_ENABLED=false`` to disable. |
| `reconnection_config` | `ReconnectionConfig \| None` | No | WebSocket reconnection behavior. |
| `telemetry` | [`TelemetryOptions`](#telemetryoptions) \| None | No | Internal worker metadata reported to the engine. |
| `worker_description` | `str \| None` | No | One-line, human/LLM-readable summary of what this worker does. Surfaces in ``engine::workers::list`` / ``engine::workers::info``. |
| `worker_name` | `str \| None` | No | Display name for this worker. A non-empty ``III_WORKER_NAME`` overrides it. Defaults to ``hostname:pid``. |

#### InvocationContext

The invocation the current code runs in, in every handler, remote or local.

Returned by ``iii.current_invocation()``.

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `caller` | `dict[str, Any] \| None` | No | Who started it: ``\{worker_id, worker_name, function_id?, invocation_id?, parent?\}``; ``None`` when unknown. |
| `function_id` | `str` | Yes | The function whose handler is running. |
| `invocation_id` | `str` | Yes | This invocation's id. |
| `observe_depth` | `int` | No | Depth of the causal chain in observe hops (0 outside any activation). |

#### MatchKeys

``on_observer_match`` as keys: an observer wants a call when they share
a key, and the SDK keeps an index instead of asking every observer.

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `call` | Callable[[[`Call`](#call)[Any, Any]], Key] | Yes | What a call is, computed once per call; a raise matches no observer. |
| `observer` | Callable[[[`Observer`](#observer)], Key] | Yes | What an observer listens for, computed once when it is accepted; an observer whose keys raise is rejected (``OBSERVE_REJECTED``). |

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `context` | `dict[str, Any]` | Yes | Auth context returned by the auth function for this session. |

default). Fields not in the observer's ``capture`` are absent.

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `activation_id` | `str` | No | - |
| `caller` | [`Caller`](#caller) | No | - |
| `duration_ms` | `float` | No | - |
| `error` | `dict[str, Any]` | No | - |

#### Observer

An observer as the worker that hosts its function sees it
(``on_observer_added``, ``observers()``, a deliver hook's ``observers``):
what was asked for. Never who observes, the observer's metadata or its
policy.

The object stays the same for the observer's whole lifetime, so a worker
keeps it in its own index (route table, consumers, ...).

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `accepted` | `(timeout: float \| None = None) -> None` | Yes | Blocks until the SDK has acked this observer: a call made afterwards reaches an active observer. Use it to send a new observer its initial state, outside its ``on_observer_added`` (which runs before the ack): a call of the function with ``"metadata": \{"for_observer": obs.id\}``, which the function's match hook gives to this observer alone, delivered like every call. Use `accepted_async` in async code. |
| `accepted_async` | `async () -> None` | Yes | Waits until the SDK has acked this observer (on any event loop). |
| `args` | `dict[str, Any]` | No | The observer's args, validated against ``args_format`` by the engine. |
| `capture` | `list[str]` | No | What travels to the target when iii delivers. |
| `filters` | `dict[str, Any]` | No | The observer's filters, normalized; iii's delivery and `matches` apply them. |
| `function_id` | `str` | No | The observed function (one this worker hosts). |
| `id` | `str` | No | The observer's id. |
| `matches` | `(call: CallLike) -> bool` | Yes | Whether ``call`` passes this observer's ``on`` and filters: what iii's delivery checks, for a deliver hook that calls targets itself. |
| `on` | `str` | No | ``success``, ``error`` or ``complete``. |
| `reject` | `(code: str, message: str) -> None` | Yes | Late rejection of an active observer (e.g. after a config reload). |
| `target` | `str` | No | The target function id. |
| `to_dict` | `() -> dict[str, Any]` | Yes | - |

---

#### ObserverHandle

What ``iii.observe`` returns, synchronously.

The observer is replayed with the same id on every reconnect until it is
disposed. The engine's refusal of its ``observe`` is final: the engine
holds nothing for it, and it is not replayed. State listeners are called in order, on a callback thread of the
SDK (never on the event loop that reads the engine's frames), so they may
call the sync API.

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dispose` | `() -> None` | Yes | Removes the observer (``unobserve``). It is not replayed on reconnect. |
| `dispose_async` | `async () -> None` | Yes | The async form of `dispose` (it does not wait for the engine). |
| `id` | `Any` | No | The observer's id (stable across replays). |
| `on_state_change` | `(listener: StateListener) -> Callable[[], None]` | Yes | Calls ``listener(state, reason)`` on every state change, in order, on the SDK's callback thread. Returns the unsubscribe function. |
| `ready` | `(timeout: float \| None = None) -> None` | Yes | Blocks until the observer is ``active``. Use `ready_async` in async code. |
| `ready_async` | `async () -> None` | Yes | Waits until the observer is ``active`` (on any event loop). |
| `reason` | `ObserveReason \| None` | Yes | Why the observer is in its state (``error``, ``suspended``, ``disposed``). |
| `state` | `ObserverState` | Yes | ``pending``, ``active``, ``suspended``, ``error`` or ``disposed``. |

---

#### ObserverOptions

The observer itself: its id, policy and metadata (the third argument of ``iii.observe``).

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `expires_in_ms` | `int` | No | Disposed after this long. |
| `id` | `str` | No | Default: a random UUID, stable across replays. |
| `max_fires` | `int` | No | Disposed after this many activations. |
| `max_in_flight` | `int` | No | Activations running at once (the engine queues the rest). |
| `metadata` | `dict[str, Any]` | No | Delivered as the metadata sidecar of every activation. |

---

#### ObserveSource

The left side of ``iii.observe``: what is observed.

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `function_id` | `str` | Yes | The observed function. |
| `args` | `dict[str, Any]` | No | For the worker that hosts the function, which reads them in its hooks; validated against the function's ``args_format``. A function without ``args_format`` takes none. |
| `capture` | `list[Capture]` | No | Default ``["input", "output", "caller"]``. |
| `deliver` | `Literal['envelope', 'input', 'output']` | No | What the target receives when iii delivers: ``"envelope"`` (default), ``"input"`` or ``"output"``. |
| `filters` | `Filter` | No | Which calls reach the target; ``\{\}`` (or absent) = every call. |
| `namespace` | `str` | No | Defaults to this worker's (``engine::*`` resolves to ``default``). |
| `on` | `Literal['success', 'error', 'complete']` | No | ``"success"`` (default), ``"error"`` or ``"complete"``. |

### iii.errors

[`InvocationError`](#invocationerror) · [`ObserveRejection`](#observerejection) · [`RegistrationRejectedError`](#registrationrejectederror)

#### InvocationError

Raised when an invocation dispatched by the SDK fails.

Inspect ``err.code`` to react to a specific category (e.g.
``'FORBIDDEN'`` for RBAC denials, ``'TIMEOUT'`` for timeouts). Catch
this class to handle every rejection. ``except Exception`` continues to
work because ``InvocationError`` inherits from ``Exception``.

Attributes are read-only after construction. ``stacktrace`` is the
engine-side trace when the remote handler raised; it may include
internal file paths and should not be surfaced to end users. ``str(err)``
intentionally never includes the stacktrace.

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | `Any` | No | - |
| `function_id` | `Any` | No | - |
| `invocation_id` | `Any` | No | - |
| `message` | `Any` | No | - |
| `stacktrace` | `Any` | No | - |

---

#### ObserveRejection

Rejects an observer with a code of its own.

Raise it from an ``on_observer_added`` hook, at either level
(``HTTP_ROUTE_CONFLICT``, ``INVALID_CRON_EXPRESSION``, ...); any other
exception rejects the observer with ``OBSERVE_REJECTED``. Raised from an
``on_observer_deliver`` hook, its code is the error the caller gets. Also
what ``ObserverHandle.ready()`` and ``Observer.accepted()`` raise when the
observer turns ``error`` or ``disposed``, with the engine's or the hook's
code (``INVALID_ARGS``, ``FORBIDDEN``, ``UNSUPPORTED``, ...).

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | `Any` | No | - |
| `message` | `Any` | No | - |

---

#### RegistrationRejectedError

Raised when the engine rejects this worker's registration.

The engine pushes a ``registrationrejected`` message and closes the
connection on a registration collision (e.g. another live worker already
owns ``(namespace, worker_name)``). This is fatal: the SDK does not
reconnect. Inspect the attributes to identify the conflict.

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | `Any` | No | - |
| `namespace` | `Any` | No | - |
| `owner_worker_id` | `Any` | No | - |
| `worker_name` | `Any` | No | - |

### iii.protocol

[`CallRequest`](#callrequest) · [`MessageType`](#messagetype) · [`RegisterFunctionFormat`](#registerfunctionformat) · [`RegisterFunctionInput`](#registerfunctioninput) · [`RegisterFunctionMessage`](#registerfunctionmessage) · [`SDK_FEATURES`](#sdk_features)

#### CallRequest

Request object for ``call()`` / ``call_async()``.

Name the function to call with ``function_id``, or call through an
observer with ``observer``: the call runs the observer's target, and only
the worker that hosts the observed function may make it.

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | [`CallActionEnqueue`](#callactionenqueue) \| [`CallActionVoid`](#callactionvoid) \| None | No | Sets how the call is routed. Omit for a synchronous request/response. Specify for a specific routing scheme (e.g. ``CallAction.Enqueue(...)``, ``CallAction.Void()``). |
| `dispatch` | `Literal['auto', 'remote'] \| None` | No | ``auto`` (default) runs a function this worker hosts in-process once the engine confirmed it; ``remote`` always goes through the engine. |
| `function_id` | `str \| None` | No | ID of the function to call. |
| `metadata` | `Any \| None` | No | Per-invocation metadata (any JSON value) supplied to the called handler beside the payload. ``None`` is no metadata. |
| `namespace` | `str \| None` | No | Target namespace for routing. Omit to inherit this worker's; say ``default`` to reach the engine's from a namespaced worker. |
| `observer` | `Any` | No | An `Observer` of a function this worker hosts: the call runs its target, with its policy and metadata sidecar. Takes no ``function_id``, ``namespace``, ``metadata`` or enqueue action. |
| `payload` | `Any` | No | Input data passed to the function. |
| `timeout_ms` | `int \| None` | No | Override the default invocation timeout, in milliseconds. |

### iii.runtime

[`FunctionRef`](#functionref)

#### FunctionRef

A registered function: the client's hook methods with its id filled in,
its observers, and ``unregister()``.

Each hook method works as a decorator and as a plain call, returns the
hook, and removes the hook when given ``None``. Hooks are stored by
function id, so they stay in place across ``unregister()`` and a later
registration of the same id.

The SDK loop runs on a thread of its own, so the engine may announce an
observer before a hook set here is in place: ``on_observer_added`` then
runs for that observer after it became active, and a warning says so.
For ``on_observer_added`` and ``on_observer_removed`` to run for every
observer, set them on the client by id before ``register_function``.

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `Any` | No | The function's id. |
| `is_observed` | `(call: CallLike \| None = None) -> bool` | Yes | Whether a call would reach anyone (see ``III.is_observed``). |
| `observers` | () -&gt; list[[`Observer`](#observer)] | Yes | The function's active observers, as this worker sees them. |
| `on_observer_added` | `(hook: AddedHook \| None) -> AddedHook \| None` | Yes | This function's ``on_observer_added`` (see ``III.on_observer_added``). |
| `on_observer_deliver` | `(hook: DeliverHook \| None) -> DeliverHook \| None` | Yes | This function's ``on_observer_deliver`` (see ``III.on_observer_deliver``). |
| `on_observer_match` | `(hook: Any = ..., *, observer: Any = None, call: Any = None) -> Any` | Yes | This function's ``on_observer_match``: a predicate ``(obs, call) -> bool``, or ``observer=`` and ``call=`` key functions (see ``III.on_observer_match``). |
| `on_observer_removed` | `(hook: RemovedHook \| None) -> RemovedHook \| None` | Yes | This function's ``on_observer_removed`` (see ``III.on_observer_removed``). |
| `unregister` | `() -> None` | Yes | Removes the function from the engine; ``on_observer_removed`` runs for each of its accepted observers. |
